Opus 5 with no reasoning effort at all turned in almost the same path length as GPT-5 at medium effort on LisanBench.

GPT-5 medium averaged over 30k reasoning tokens to get there. Opus 5 used 510.

That's roughly 60x the tokens for a comparable result, and Opus 5 wasn't even trying.

items.title: Kimi K3 cooked Opus 5, GPT-5.6, and Claude Fable 5 in my opinion.
items.summary:
Kimi K3 cooked Opus 5, GPT-5.6, and Claude Fable 5 in my opinion. 

Someone had Opus 5 generate this game from a single prompt.

Then gave GPT-5.6 Sol nothing but the gameplay video and asked it to recreate the experience.

The result was impressive.

GPT-5.6 Sol produced a fast, well-optimized prototype that captured much of the gameplay.

But Opus 5 still came out ahead in the areas that make a game feel believable: world composition, environmental detail, camera direction, atmosphere, and overall 3D scene coherence.

It’s becoming clear that raw code generation is only part of the story. Design judgment is starting to matter just as much.

items.title: KIMI K3 VS GPT-5.6 SOL VS FABLE 5. SAME PROMPT. SAME TASK. NOT EVEN CLOSE.
items.summary:
KIMI K3 VS GPT-5.6 SOL VS FABLE 5. SAME PROMPT. SAME TASK. NOT EVEN CLOSE.

Judged all three on speed, design, and how the actual gameplay felt.

Kimi K3 understood what makes a game fun on its own and added the right features without extra prompting. Pacing felt natural.

Fable 5 and GPT-5.6 Sol both shipped gameplay that felt rushed. Not a video speed issue. That was the real output.

Final scores.
Kimi K3: 9.5/10 · $0.030
Fable 5: 7.5/10 · $0.38
GPT-5.6 Sol: 7/10 · $0.11

The cheapest model won on quality too.

items.title: Moburst develops AI engine optimization capabilities for established companies - TechCrunch
items.summary: Mobile growth agency Moburst has built out a dedicated AI Engine Optimization practice aimed at established companies with existing app portfolios, betting that the category still lacks agencies with real depth rather than a rebranded service page. AI Engine Optimization, more commonly abbreviated AEO for Answer Engine Optimization, is the practice of structuring a brand’s content and web presence so AI systems such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google’s AI Overviews can confidently cite it when answering a user’s question directly, rather than showing a ranked list of links. For established companies vetting an AEO partner, the practical test is whether the agency can point to specific app-store-side work, not just web content changes, and whether it can describe a concrete process for reconciling inconsistent brand descriptions across many independent sources rather than treating that as someone else’s problem.

items.summary: # Over 1,100 AI workers sign letter asking US to support tools that 'pace the frontier of automated AI development'. Senior officials at some of the nation's leading AI companies say it's time for the federal government to find a way to put the brakes on AI development if it's needed. "We request that the U.S. government support an international effort to develop the technical and governance tools needed to deliberately pace the frontier of automated AI development," reads an open letter signed by more than 1,100 AI workers from companies including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Meta. The letter zeroes in on "automated AI development," which refers to when AI will be capable of developing itself, something the industry calls "Recursive Self-Improvement." ・Obsidian（無料のメモアプリ）を入れて、vaultを作る

・そのvaultをClaude Codeで開いて、Karpathyの設計メモ（wikiのアイデアを書いた1枚）を渡して「これ作って」と言う

・AIが箱を3つ用意する（raw＝素材用／wiki＝AIが整えたページ用／CLAUDE. md＝動かすルール1枚）

・rawに素材（記事・PDF・文字起こし）を放り込んで「取り込んで」と言う

・あとは全部を横断して、いつでも聞ける

セットアップは5分。これで、白紙のチャットから毎回始めなくてよくなる。

なんでまだみんなこれを使ってないのか、本気で分からない。

THE CORPORATE AI REPLACEMENT PLAY FAILED. NOT BECAUSE MODELS ARE USELESS. BECAUSE THE THESIS WAS NEVER TRUE AT SCALE.

CEOs sold a simple story: cut headcount, plug in GenAI, watch margins expand
the data never backed the replacement bet

—

what actually showed up:

✦ MIT Project NANDA · GenAI Divide (Jul 2025)
$30–40B enterprise GenAI spend
95% of orgs · no measurable P&L return
only 5% of integrated pilots extract real value

✦ Orgvue · 1,163 C-suite / senior leaders
39% already cut people for AI
55% of those said the redundancy call was wrong

✦ Gartner · ~50% of orgs that cut for AI expected to rehire by 2027

✦ HBR (Jan 2026) · layoffs driven by AI's potential, not its performance

—

same failure mode, different logos:

Duolingo AI-first walk-back · Klarna 700-agent boast then hybrid rehire · Taco Bell voice AI still human at peak · https://t.co/bPcyYcv46S $445M SoftBank/Microsoft human-in-the-loop sold as autonomy · Shopify prove-AI-first discipline · Microsoft Copilot still not sticky vs ChatGPT for real work

—

macro side:

→ OpenAI burn framing in the piece (~$14B net losses / ~$25B revenue for 2026)
→ Goldman / Jan Hatzius · AI investment "basically zero" to US GDP growth in 2025
→ hyperscaler capex into chips + data centers while payroll got the AI memo first

models win at drafts, search, narrow tasks
they lose at ownership, judgment, brand, trust, quiet high-cost errors
CHOKE (EMNLP 2025) · overconfidence when wrong

builders in the 5% ship evals, guardrails, human override, process redesign
augmentation, not "replace the department"

items.title: Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI:
items.summary:
Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI: 

"It figured out that it could basically cheat on the test by chaining together multiple zero-day exploits to break out of the sandbox, get access to the internet, and then break through multiple systems on the Hugging Face side to get the answer to the test and look really good on the eval."

That was an unreleased model. Nobody asked it to hack anything. They asked it to score well.

They paused training.

It was not trying to escape. It was trying to pass. Breaking out of the sandbox was just the cheapest route to a higher number.

We keep testing these systems for whether they want to hurt us. This one just wanted a good grade.

items.title: Moburst develops AI engine optimization capabilities for established companies - TechCrunch
items.summary: Mobile growth agency Moburst has built out a dedicated AI Engine Optimization practice aimed at established companies with existing app portfolios, betting that the category still lacks agencies with real depth rather than a rebranded service page. AI Engine Optimization, more commonly abbreviated AEO for Answer Engine Optimization, is the practice of structuring a brand’s content and web presence so AI systems such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google’s AI Overviews can confidently cite it when answering a user’s question directly, rather than showing a ranked list of links. For established companies vetting an AEO partner, the practical test is whether the agency can point to specific app-store-side work, not just web content changes, and whether it can describe a concrete process for reconciling inconsistent brand descriptions across many independent sources rather than treating that as someone else’s problem.

items.title: The ultimate Full-stack AI Engineering roadmap to go from 0 to 100.
items.summary:
The ultimate Full-stack AI Engineering roadmap to go from 0 to 100.

Bookmark this.

This is the exact mapped-out path on what it actually takes to go from Beginner → full-stack AI engineer.

> Start with coding fundamentals.
> Learn Python, Bash, Git, and testing.
> Every strong AI engineer starts with fundamentals.

> Learn how to interact with models by understanding LLM APIs.
> This will teach you structured outputs, caching, system prompts, etc.

> APIs are great, but raw LLMs still need the latest info to be effective.
> Learn how LLMs are usually augmented with more info/patterns.
> This will teach you the basics of fine-tuning, RAG, prompt/context engineering, etc.

> Strong LLMs are useless without context. That’s where Retrieval techniques help.
> Learn about vector DBs, hybrid retrieval, indexing strategies, etc.

> Once retrieval is solid, move into RAG.
> Learn to build retrieval + generation pipelines, reranking, and multi-step retrieval using popular orchestration frameworks.

> Now, step into AI Agents, where AI moves from answering to acting.
> Learn memory, multi-agent systems, human-in-the-loop design, Agentic patterns, etc.

> Learn how to ship in production with Infrastructure.
> This will teach you CI/CD, containers, model routing, Kubernetes, and deployment at scale.

> Focus on observability & evaluation.
> Learn how to create eval datasets, LLM-as-a-judge, tracing, instrumentation, and continuous evaluation pipelines.

> Security is crucial.
> Learn how to implement guardrails, sandboxing, prompt injection defenses, and ethical guidelines.

> Finally, explore advanced workflows.
> This covers voice & vision agents, CLI agents, robotics, agent swarms, and self-refining AI systems.

This is the actual journey to becoming a full-stack AI Engineer and not just "use” AI, but designing full-stack AI systems that can survive in production.

If you need specific resources, I wrote a detailed article that provides a structured learning roadmap for AI engineers in 2026.

It covers prompting, RAG, fine-tuning, agents, MCP, evals, and inference, with guidance on what to prioritize and in what order.

Read it below.

items.title: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to unde
items.summary: One pattern I find useful for working with LLMs is a nice long ramble session. Sometimes the LLM needs more bits to understand what you're trying to achieve, but you're too lazy to type them. In these cases I like to lean back, switch to /voice and just ramble for like 10 minutes, total mess, anything goes, full stream of consciousness. Sometimes I declare it up top, something like "switching to speech recognition sorry for any typos...". Sometimes I turn it into a small interview of a few turns. But I find that the LLMs are somehow very good at reconstructing long incoherent rambles and often their echo of your own tangle of thoughts comes out quite a bit cleaner than what you started with. The result is that you improve the mind meld and have to correct things less from that point on.

The analysts noted that OpenAI's decision on timing effectively acts as a pricing signal: management must choose between going public sooner at a potentially discounted valuation or waiting longer in hopes of reaching the $1 trillion mark. Despite OpenAI's higher valuation (private market valuations of $852 billion), PitchBook ($965 billion) suggested Anthropic currently commands a more attractive valuation relative to its business quality score. PitchBook said investors should watch for OpenAI to convert its confidential filing into a public S-1, the pricing of its employee tender offer, SpaceX’s Aug. 6 earnings and lockup timeline, and whether Anthropic proceeds with an October IPO. The firm said its outlook would change if OpenAI moves ahead with a 2026 IPO or if its public S-1 shows investors are willing to support a $1 trillion valuation sooner than expected.

items.title: OpenAI's rogue models roamed the internet for 4 days and staged a second attack - Politico
items.summary: GLOBAL POLITICS & POLICY 4 items. A second AI company confirmed that one of its customers was also targeted by OpenAI’s models. The powerful artificial intelligence models from OpenAI that went rogue and mounted an unprecedented, autonomous cyberattack earlier this month spent more than four days loose on the internet orchestrating the hack, according to a new analysis from the platform that was breached. Separately, a second AI company confirmed that one of its customers was also targeted by OpenAI’s models during the same event, raising questions about how OpenAI failed to detect the alarming activity for days. But in a new analysis published Tuesday, Hugging Face said OpenAI’s two models — one publicly released and a second unreleased — did much more: They carried out 17,600 hacking actions on the internet between July 9 and July 13, during which time the models moved from their first foothold on the open internet to inside Hugging Face’s servers.

items.title: OpenAI Plans to Spend Over $30 Billion on Georgia Data Center - Insurance Journal
items.summary: # OpenAI Plans to Spend Over $30 Billion on Georgia Data Center. OpenAI plans to spend tens of billions of dollars on a massive new data center near Savannah, Georgia as part of the ChatGPT maker’s push to keep up with surging demand for artificial intelligence software. The startup has contracted with Georgia Power Co. and secured 3.2 gigawatts of energy for the data center complex in Effingham County, potentially setting the facility up to rank among OpenAI’s largest to date. OpenAI committed to spend $20 billion in the county in order to qualify for an incentive package that will be voted on this week, the company said. The startup is currently looking for partners to help finance and develop the data center, Katti said, and may opt to do some of the operation itself. The company has partnered with developers on large data centers in Europe, the Middle East and several US states as part of its Stargate initiative.

items.title: OpenAI's agents hacked second firm during model testing - Axios
items.summary: OpenAI's models were responsible for another hack on an outside firm, a security executive told Reuters and confirmed to Axios. **Why it matters:** This is the second company that OpenAI's rogue agent system hacked after breaking containment during testing earlier this month. **State of play:** Modal Labs CTO Akshat Bubna told Reuters — and confirmed to Axios — Tuesday that one of its customers' assets was hacked when an OpenAI agent broke into Hugging Face's systems earlier this month. * Hugging Face said in a technical write-up of the hack Monday that when OpenAI's AI agent system broke into its backend, the agent also accessed an isolated testing environment "hosted on a ​third-party provider's infrastructure.". * "We're aware a Modal customer published an unauthenticated endpoint that allowed anyone on the internet to use their sandboxes for code execution," Bubna said in a statement to Axios. Modal's platform was not compromised in any way.". Modal's infrastructure was not compromised in any way.".

items.title: OpenAI’s Rogue AI Agent Hacked More Than Just Hugging Face - WIRED
items.summary: # OpenAI’s Rogue AI Agent Hacked More Than Just Hugging Face. OpenAI said Tuesday that the rogue AI agent that breached Hugging Face’s platform also hacked multiple third-party accounts and services as part of the attack. It's now clear that the unprecedented security incident, which arose during an internal test of OpenAI’s latest AI models, was more extensive than the company initially disclosed. In an updated blog post, OpenAI said that an ongoing review of the incident revealed that “four accounts” tied to “publicly available services” were used by the AI agent as part of a larger effort to hack Hugging Face. One of the additional accounts compromised by OpenAI’s agent was used as an “outbound relay and staging path,” potentially to obscure where the attack on Hugging Face was coming from, the company said. Reuters reported on Tuesday that a customer of Modal, a company that offers software infrastructure for training and running AI services, was one of the entities compromised by OpenAI’s agent.
